title: Customer 360: an account page built from your own content
description: One page per account — status, risks, and a drill-in chat — assembled from whatever your instance already knows about that customer. No CRM export, no separate index.
prerequisites: An OAuth access token or Glean API token with the SEARCH and CHAT scopes
X_GLEAN_INCLUDE_EXPERIMENTAL=true set (the Platform API is Experimental as of its 2026-07 launch)
An account name your instance has content about — the app is built around it
Node 20+, and a page you can serve with a small server so the token stays server-side

demoQueries.query: What's the status of our renewal with that account?
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: Returns a non-empty answer citing real documents about the account you built the page around. Substitute the account name when you ask it — the page is built around whichever one you pick, so there is no fixed query text here.
Synthesizes across more than one source, with a citation per claim, rather than restating a single document.
Either names risks grounded in cited content, or says it has none to report. It must not infer risk the sources don't support — an account with no recorded risk is a real answer, not a gap to fill.

steps.title: Pick a path
steps.description: Path A (Platform Search + Chat) builds an open-ended explorable dashboard: parallel search.query tiles and POST /api/chat for journey summary and saved prompts. Path B (Platform Agents) keeps the same page UX but runs synthesis through glean.agents.createRun against a template Account Brief agent.

aiPrompt:
Build a Customer 360 account page on Glean following
https://developers.glean.com/cookbook/customer-360

1. Ask me which path: (A) Platform Search + Chat or (B) Platform Agents.
   Build the one I pick. Do NOT use Client API chat.create,
   client.search.query, or client.agents.run.
2. Ask me which account to build the page around, and which of my own
   sources cover it. Do not invent an account, and do not hardcode
   figures like ARR, seat count or renewal date — read them from
   retrieval, and leave a field blank when nothing supports it.
3. Layout: a KPI header, source tiles for the retrieved documents, a
   synthesized journey summary, saved-prompt buttons, and a drill-in
   chat. Empty tiles read "no recent activity" rather than "0".
4. Path A: parallel glean.search.query calls for the tiles; summary
   and follow-ups via a server-side POST /api/chat with
   { input, stream: false, store: true } and
   X_GLEAN_INCLUDE_EXPERIMENTAL. Parse output_text plus
   annotations[].sources[]. The token never reaches the browser.
5. Path B: same page; synthesis via glean.agents.createRun({ messages,
   stream: false }, GLEAN_AGENT_ID). Document the Agent Builder
   prerequisite, and degrade gracefully if the agent is missing or
   unauthorized rather than failing the page.
6. Whatever the path: when retrieval returns nothing for a tile or a
   prompt, say so. Never let the model answer from its own knowledge —
   a confident, uncited claim about a real customer is the worst
   possible output for this app.
7. Style it per the house style below: the real Glean logomark, Glean
   Blue (#343ced) as the accent.
8. Verify with the demo queries against the account I chose.
llmContext: Platform-only recipe. Search: glean.search.query -> POST /api/search, results[].title/url/snippets (string[]). Chat: fetch POST /api/chat (until glean.chat.create ships); request {input, stream:false, store:true}; response output[].content[] type=output_text with annotations[].sources[]. Agents: glean.agents.createRun(request, agentId) -> POST /api/agents/{agent_id}/runs; stream:false returns PlatformAgentRunWaitResponse synchronously (no polling); messages use role USER|GLEAN_AI and content[{text,type:text}]. Experimental opt-in via X_GLEAN_INCLUDE_EXPERIMENTAL. Do NOT teach glean.client.chat.create, glean.client.search.query, or glean.client.agents.run. Tokens server-side only. The account and its facts come from the reader's own instance: nothing here may hardcode an account name, ARR, seat count or renewal date. An earlier draft of this recipe was written against a demo corpus that no longer exists, which made the page display one fictional customer's numbers regardless of what was retrieved. Treat an empty retrieval as a first-class state and render it as such -- for an app that speaks about named customers, an uncited claim is worse than a blank field.
